title: Echoes Within: Perceptions & Reality
description: Explore shifts in perception and thought that shape your inner world.

questions.text: In the quiet moments, or even amidst the everyday hum, have you recently found yourself perceiving things that others around you don't seem to notice – perhaps a voice, a fleeting image, or an unusual sensation that feels intensely real?

options.text: No, my perceptions feel entirely aligned with shared reality.
Occasionally, there's a brief, ambiguous sense of something, but it's rarely disruptive and I can usually dismiss it.
Yes, I experience these perceptions with some regularity, and they sometimes cause me distress or make it harder to focus.
These vivid perceptions are a frequent and powerful part of my experience, making it profoundly difficult to distinguish what's real from what isn't, often disrupting my daily life.

insight_cloud.title: The Mind's Canvas
insight_cloud.text: Hallucinations are sensory experiences that appear real but are created by your mind, often related to various conditions, not solely psychosis. They can involve any of the five senses and vary greatly in intensity and impact on daily functioning.

questions.text: Have you recently held beliefs that feel unshakably true to you, even when others present strong evidence to the contrary, or when these beliefs seem quite unusual compared to common understanding?

options.text: My beliefs generally align with shared reality and I am open to new information.
Occasionally, I might have an unusual idea, but I can usually question it or understand different perspectives.
Yes, I hold certain firm beliefs that others find unusual or difficult to accept, which sometimes causes friction or misunderstanding.
These unwavering beliefs profoundly dominate my thoughts, making it nearly impossible to consider other viewpoints, often leading to significant distress or impacting my relationships and actions.

questions.text: When you express your thoughts, or even internally when you think, do you find your ideas sometimes jumbled, hard to follow, or jump unexpectedly between unrelated topics, making clear communication a struggle?

options.text: My thoughts and speech flow clearly and logically, making communication easy.
Sometimes my thoughts feel a little scattered, especially under stress, but I can usually re-center myself.
Yes, I often notice my thoughts or speech becoming somewhat disorganized, occasionally making it hard for others to understand me, and sometimes causing me frustration.
My thoughts and speech frequently become so fragmented or illogical that conveying my ideas or understanding others is profoundly difficult, severely impairing my ability to communicate effectively.

questions.text: Have you noticed a significant dimming of your inner spark – perhaps a profound decrease in motivation, a flattening of emotions, or a loss of interest in activities and connections that once brought you joy and purpose?

options.text: My motivation, emotional expression, and interest in life feel vibrant and consistent.
I occasionally feel less motivated or a bit flat, but these feelings are temporary and don't significantly impact my life.
Yes, I often experience a notable reduction in motivation, emotional range, or interest in things I once enjoyed, making daily tasks and connections feel effortful.
This profound withdrawal of motivation, emotional expression, and joy is pervasive, making it overwhelmingly difficult to engage in life, form connections, or pursue any meaningful activity.

questions.text: Do you frequently struggle with focusing your attention, remembering important details, or solving everyday problems, making even routine tasks feel overwhelming and draining?

options.text: My attention, memory, and problem-solving skills feel sharp and reliable.
I sometimes have minor lapses in concentration or memory, but these are brief and don't significantly affect my performance.
Yes, I often find myself struggling to maintain focus, recall information, or think clearly, which causes noticeable difficulty in my daily responsibilities.

My ability to concentrate, retain new information, or make decisions is severely compromised, making it nearly impossible to manage daily life or engage in complex activities without significant support.

insight_cloud.title: The Brain's Symphony
insight_cloud.text: Cognitive difficulties, such as those with attention, memory, and executive function, are common across many mental health conditions, including psychosis. They can profoundly affect daily functioning and are often a target for therapeutic interventions.
